text.p: Bonds extended gains of Monday, taking their lead from the rest of Europe, but volumes were thinned by holiday absences, traders said.
They said that the market were also waiting for confirmation of expectations that the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee will leave rates unchanged when it meets later on Tuesday.
The 20 basis point rate cut by the Bank of Portugal on Monday helped narrow spreads slightly with Germany and neighbouring Spain.
"The market is firmer (and) the trend is upwards, despite the lack of liquidity," said one trader.
"The affect of the rate cut (by the central bank) has not yet been exhausted. Bonds have room to perform better than the Bunds," added another trader.
Traders said that interest was beginning to focus on the shorter end of the curve which should benefit most from the rate cut.
